clue.text: The lexicographer who broke our seals

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so the letters of these two words are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A dictionary-maker caused damage to some marine animals belonging to us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' rearranges OURSEALS. Pierre Larousse was the French compiler of the famous dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre Larousse was a nineteenth-century French dictionary compiler, whose name lives on in his publishing house.

clue.text: Will such a policy shorten school holidays?

definitions.text: Will such a policy shorten school holidays?

parts.words: Will such a policy shorten school holidays?
parts.note: a policy for the distant future, read as making a school's teaching period lengthier

explanation.surface: Asking whether a plan will cut the children's vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: British schools have three terms; a lengthier term leaves shorter holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy planned to cover a lengthy future period.

clue.text: Let it start to pour, nothing in it, Max, you say'

annotationWithheld.why: Let it start to pour, nothing in it, Max, you say' (9): OCR text seems garbled; 'Max, you say' suggests macs, but no clean parse of the rest gives RAINCOATS
annotationWithheld.clue: Let it start to pour, nothing in it, Max, you say'

clue.text: Bear genus is upper-class USSR variety

indicators.note: a variety of the letters is a different arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A bear's scientific family name is a Soviet blend of social classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges USSR into RSUS after U.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursus is the Latin scientific name for the genus of big brown and black bears.

clue.text: Library books thus put aside

definitions.meaning: books in a library sit on racks in this way
postponed or set aside for later

explanation.definitionFit: Books are placed on shelves in a library; a postponed plan is likewise set aside.

clue.text: Dad has' brushed-back hair — the outsider!

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for a father

indicators.note: hair brushed back is turned the other way, so the word hair is read backwards

parts.note: taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: Father, with his hair combed backwards, is an outcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brushed-back' turns HAIR into RIAH, placed after PA.
explanation.definitionFit: A pariah is a social outcast, someone shunned by society.

clue.text: A writer leads numbers of snappy dressers 'to ' the mountains

parts.note: a pen is something to write with
smart dressers are dressed up to the nines, so the number is nines

explanation.surface: An author introduces stylish people to the mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads' places A PEN ahead of NINES; 'dressed to the nines' means very smartly dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the mountain chain running down the length of Italy.

clue.text: Still interchangeable

indicators.note: letters that are changeable can be rearranged, here the first five letters of the clue's single word

explanation.surface: Something remains capable of being swapped.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word splits as INTER + CHANGEABLE; 'changeable' rearranges INTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something motionless and inactive is said to be still.

clue.text: How Spooner's truants disapproved of the mystery lesson?

definitions.text: How Spooner's truants disapproved of the mystery lesson?

parts.words: How Spooner's truants disapproved of the mystery lesson?
parts.note: truants miss the history lesson; with the opening sounds swapped they hiss the mystery lesson, and one who hisses shows disapproval

explanation.surface: Pupils skipping a puzzling class showed their dislike.
explanation.walkthrough: Spooner swapped opening sounds: 'miss history' becomes 'hiss mystery'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone expressing disapproval with a sibilant sound, as an audience does at a villain.

clue.text: Stiffener for street support

parts.note: an arch supports a bridge or building

explanation.surface: A brace for a road holding up something.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is used to stiffen collars and fabric.

clue.text: They get hit on the head in the drive-in

definitions.text: They get hit on the head in the drive-in

parts.words: They get hit on the head in the drive-in
parts.note: a drive-in sounds like an open-air cinema, but read literally it is the act of hammering things in, each struck on its flat top

explanation.surface: Moviegoers at an outdoor cinema get assaulted.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpentry fasteners are driven into wood by hammer blows on their heads.

clue.text: Dainty stopgap

definitions.meaning: a dainty is a delicacy, a small sweet dish
something filling a gap, here the side dish served between main courses

explanation.definitionFit: The French culinary term names a light sweet or side dish served between courses, filling the interval at a meal.

clue.text: Just keeps going when there's no more credit

definitions.meaning: an engine idling runs steadily without moving the car
tick is slang for credit, and when it is finished it is over

explanation.surface: Someone muddles along once their money has run out.
explanation.definitionFit: An idling engine runs slowly; read as a phrase, tick (credit) is finished.

clue.text: Chemical change of 7

indicators.note: a change of letters shuffles them into a different order

parts.note: the answer to 7 down, a word meaning still

explanation.surface: A chemical transformation of some substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of' rearranges INERT, the answer to 7 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is a chemical compound used in gunpowder and fertiliser.

clue.text: Foundation on track of vagrant's sleeping quarters?

definitions.meaning: the base layer on which a railway or road is laid
a tramp sleeps rough on the highway, so the street is his bed

explanation.definitionFit: The base for a railway's sleepers or a road surface; jokingly, where a tramp lies down on the street.

clue.text: Given for what's bound to be one's choice

definitions.text: Given for what's bound to be one's choice

parts.words: Given for what's bound to be one's choice
parts.note: bound refers to a volume in covers: a gift voucher redeemable for a volume the recipient picks

explanation.surface: A present for whatever you are sure to select.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift voucher exchangeable in a bookshop for a volume of the recipient's choosing.

clue.text: The horse to watch

definitions.meaning: a strong horse bred for riding to hounds
a pocket watch with a hinged lid protecting its face

explanation.definitionFit: A breed of horse used for fox-hunting, and a pocket timepiece with a protective cover.

clue.text: The place where ground rent originated?

definitions.text: The place where ground rent originated?

parts.words: The place where ground rent originated?
parts.note: ground rent sounds like a property charge, but here the ground is torn by an earthquake, and this is where the rupture begins

explanation.surface: Asking where the leasehold charge on land first arose.
explanation.definitionFit: The point on the surface directly above an earthquake's origin.

clue.text: Dealer about to take a manager

parts.note: C, from circa, means about
a handler manages an animal or a boxer

explanation.surface: A trader is set to hire an executive.
explanation.definitionFit: A chandler is a dealer in supplies, such as a ship's chandler.

clue.text: Classify varieties of rats so

indicators.note: varieties are different versions, so the letters of these words take a new form

explanation.surface: Sort different kinds of rodent in this way.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort things is to group them by type, which is to classify them.

clue.text: Row in a race? On the contrary. (Bit of a laugh I)

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other; the following words swap which goes inside which

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race

explanation.surface: Is a rower in a race? No, the reverse, and it's a giggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips 'row in race': TT goes inside TIER instead. The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: A titter is a short suppressed laugh, a giggle.

clue.text: Was shipwrecked, became virulent

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a wrecked ship is broken up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor lost at sea turned bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' turns SHIP into PISH, after WAS; 'became' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sharply spiteful and stinging in manner is akin to being venomous or virulent.

clue.text: Aspiring women's leader has double trouble

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the opening letter of the word women's
to trouble is to disturb, so the letters of double are stirred up

explanation.surface: A head of a women's group faces twice the problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges DOUBLE into OULDBE after W.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hopeful of becoming something is ambitious, or aspiring.

clue.text: Thanks to Pierre, a part of old England

parts.note: merci is French for thank you, as a Frenchman like Pierre would say

explanation.surface: Gratitude to a Frenchman for a region of historic England.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom of the English Midlands.

clue.text: Record, thing done in this lunar age

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
an act is a deed, a thing done

explanation.surface: We keep records of deeds in this moon-dominated era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ACT inside EP. An epact is the moon's age on New Year's Day, used for calculating Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: The epact is the number of days in the moon's phase at the start of the calendar year.

clue.text: Tavern widow's farewell

annotationWithheld.why: Tavern widow's farewell (5): no parse of 'Tavern widow's' gives A DIEU; the OCR text may be garbled

clue.text: Short staff of policemen

parts.note: looks like a complaint about too few officers, but it describes the short club carried by the police

explanation.surface: The police force is understaffed.
explanation.definitionFit: A police baton is a short stick carried by officers.

clue.text: What pattern of cloth, mate ?

parts.note: a chequered fabric pattern, and the chess word that comes before mate

explanation.surface: Asking a friend what design the material has.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern of squares on fabric, and the chess warning that precedes a final mate.

clue.text: Successor to egg-plant in a neglected garden?

definitions.text: Successor to egg-plant in a neglected garden?

parts.words: Successor to egg-plant in a neglected garden?
parts.note: the aubergine is a decoy: what comes after an egg is a young bird, and an unwanted growth in an untended plot is a weed

explanation.surface: Something growing after the aubergines in an overgrown plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A common small weed of untended ground, its name joining a young bird and an unwanted plant.

clue.text: Praise the former lot in retrospect

parts.note: ex is a prefix meaning former

indicators.note: looking back means the word lot is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Commend the previous group, looking back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retrospect' turns LOT into TOL, after EX.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud someone is to praise them highly.

clue.text: Does this old girl …

parts.note: an old girl in the school sense is a former pupil, a female graduate

explanation.surface: Asking whether a former schoolgirl does something, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue runs on into 30 across: does a former schoolgirl recognise a former schoolboy by his tie?
explanation.definitionFit: A female former student of a school or university.

clue.text: . recognize the old boy by his this?

definitions.text: recognize the old boy by his this?

parts.words: recognize the old boy by his this?
parts.note: old boys of a school are identified by their distinctive school tie

explanation.surface: Continuing 29 across: is a former pupil identified by what he wears?
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues from 29 across. In Britain an 'old school tie' marks former pupils of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Ties and scarves are worn around the throat, and a school tie identifies its old boys.
